title: 25 FOR REASONS
subtitle: A college-football poll with receipts.
question: If everybody played next Saturday, which 25 teams would we believe in most?

cadence.review: Each published edition dates its evidence and keeps the previous board.
cadence.next: Next edition after the next results review; no automatic publication is promised.

methodology.label: Strength
methodology.note: Who we would trust on a neutral field next Saturday.

methodology.label: Continuity
methodology.note: Quarterback, line, coordinator, and returning-production evidence.

methodology.label: Path
methodology.note: Schedule leverage and the real route into the 12-team playoff.

methodology.label: Accountability
methodology.note: Every case, doubt, and proof stays attached to the team all season.

sale.name: PointCast 25 / 2026 Founding Season Ticket
sale.promise: Back the complete 2026 editorial season. The ranking and its receipts remain public; the ticket funds the weekly research, audio dispatches, and permanent season ledger.

movementBaseline: Board 000 · July 27, 2026. No intervening PointCast boards were published.
editorialNote: PointCast rankings are editorial judgments. Records and latest results are sourced separately; the AP comparison is the September 20 poll. This edition does not imply live scores or an automated weekly update.

teams.reason: The lead belongs to Texas; now make it travel.
teams.case: A 3–0 start and the national No. 1 position put the burden of proof on the challenger.
teams.doubt: Routine control at home does not settle the next difficult road game.
teams.proof: Keep the offense functional when the crowd and the early score turn against it.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #3 → #1. The lead belongs to Texas; now make it travel.

teams.reason: A convincing road result earns the second chair.
teams.case: The Arkansas margin gives this week’s case a conference result away from home.
teams.doubt: One comfortable SEC afternoon is not a complete assessment of the defense.
teams.proof: Repeat that control against an opponent capable of forcing a close fourth quarter.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #5 → #2. A convincing road result earns the second chair.

teams.reason: We were too low. The succession argument now has a scoreboard.
teams.case: Beating LSU supplies stronger evidence than July anxiety about the coaching transition.
teams.doubt: An emotional home win must become a repeatable standard.
teams.proof: Carry the same composure into the next road test.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #17 → #3. We were too low. The succession argument now has a scoreboard.

teams.reason: Still in the title conversation; this week we reward the sharper SEC evidence.
teams.case: A seventeen-point win keeps the undefeated start intact.
teams.doubt: Being dependable is different from demonstrating the highest ceiling.
teams.proof: Win a game where the opponent forces the offense to change its first plan.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #2 → #4. Still in the title conversation; this week we reward the sharper SEC evidence.

teams.reason: A road conference win matters more than an immaculate-looking home score.
teams.case: Miami leaves Wake Forest unbeaten with thirteen points of separation.
teams.doubt: Twenty points conceded leave a defensive question underneath the win.
teams.proof: Produce a complete defensive afternoon against a more demanding attack.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #7 → #5. A road conference win matters more than an immaculate-looking home score.

teams.reason: The champion is handling its work; the next measuring stick must be taller.
teams.case: A shutout preserves the unbeaten start and earns continued title-level trust.
teams.doubt: A clean result against this opposition cannot settle the top-five order.
teams.proof: Keep the same control when explosive plays are harder to find.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #6 → #6. The champion is handling its work; the next measuring stick must be taller.

teams.reason: The ceiling survives. The preseason No. 1 entitlement does not.
teams.case: A decisive response keeps Ohio State firmly in the contender group.
teams.doubt: A rebound rout does not erase the loss already on the record.
teams.proof: Close the next high-level contest without needing a perfect passing afternoon.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #1 → #7. The ceiling survives. The preseason No. 1 entitlement does not.

teams.reason: Road production moves BYU ahead of our July caution.
teams.case: An eighteen-point road win strengthens the case for a place in our first eight.
teams.doubt: Allowing 23 keeps the defensive transition under review.
teams.proof: Win when the offense cannot reach forty.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #16 → #8. Road production moves BYU ahead of our July caution.

teams.reason: Fifty points buy attention. Thirty-six allowed keep the receipt open.
teams.case: The offense supplied enough to preserve an unbeaten record.
teams.doubt: A shootout is not evidence that the whole team has become physically controlling.
teams.proof: Win a competitive game without needing a fifty-point rescue.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #11 → #9. Fifty points buy attention. Thirty-six allowed keep the receipt open.

teams.reason: Survival counts, but two points are not separation.
teams.case: Texas Tech protected its unbeaten record against a ranked conference opponent.
teams.doubt: The narrow margin leaves less room for certainty than the record suggests.
teams.proof: Create a clear advantage against the next serious conference test.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #9 → #10. Survival counts, but two points are not separation.

teams.reason: Oxford turns the installation story into an accountability story.
teams.case: Losing by eight at a top-five opponent leaves a plausible contender case.
teams.doubt: The July ceiling has not yet become a dependable close-game operation.
teams.proof: Finish the next tight conference game with a coherent final possession.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #8 → #11. Oxford turns the installation story into an accountability story.

teams.reason: Four wins are real. So is the defensive bill.
teams.case: A one-score road conference win is useful evidence of survival.
teams.doubt: Thirty-five conceded makes control a harder claim than the record alone suggests.
teams.proof: Close a strong opponent out without another shootout.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #10 → #12. Four wins are real. So is the defensive bill.

teams.reason: The post-Whittingham floor looks sturdier than our opening board allowed.
teams.case: A rivalry shutout gives the developmental-continuity thesis an encouraging result.
teams.doubt: This score does not establish the ceiling against the best Big 12 offenses.
teams.proof: Carry that defensive discipline into a genuinely demanding conference game.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #20 → #13. The post-Whittingham floor looks sturdier than our opening board allowed.

teams.reason: The assembled roster is winning. Its hardest chemistry test is still ahead.
teams.case: An unbeaten start and a wide latest margin justify keeping Penn State near the playoff tier.
teams.doubt: Buffalo cannot answer every question about execution under pressure.
teams.proof: Show the same connection on third down in a close conference game.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #12 → #14. The assembled roster is winning. Its hardest chemistry test is still ahead.

teams.reason: The opening work is complete; the credibility test gets larger now.
teams.case: A 33-point win gives Tennessee a clean result to carry forward.
teams.doubt: This opposition cannot certify quarterback decisions against a contender.
teams.proof: Keep possessions stable when an elite opponent removes the easy throw.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #18 → #15. The opening work is complete; the credibility test gets larger now.

teams.reason: A ranked win earns a seat that the preseason board did not reserve.
teams.case: Beating SMU by ten supplies a concrete reason to enter the board.
teams.doubt: One strong result does not remove the loss or the defensive questions.
teams.proof: Back up the breakthrough with a second complete conference performance.
teams.movementReason: New to PointCast 25. A ranked win earns a seat that the preseason board did not reserve.

teams.reason: The offense has supplied a number worth noticing; the opponent limits the inference.
teams.case: A shutout and fifty-five points are a useful opening signal.
teams.doubt: An FCS result is not proof that the old offensive constraints are gone.
teams.proof: Move the ball when a conference defense can challenge every easy yard.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #25 → #17. The offense has supplied a number worth noticing; the opponent limits the inference.

teams.reason: A road SEC win moves the reset beyond a press-conference promise.
teams.case: Winning at Auburn is enough to put Florida above our opening slot.
teams.doubt: Thirty-nine conceded is a substantial warning attached to the celebration.
teams.proof: Follow the breakthrough with a win that does not require forty-plus points.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #22 → #18. A road SEC win moves the reset beyond a press-conference promise.

teams.reason: The unbeaten start keeps Michigan in view; the next comparison must be tougher.
teams.case: The latest margin shows a team handling its scheduled work.
teams.doubt: UTEP does not settle the difficult questions about the new operation.
teams.proof: Make the offense coherent against a defense that can force long downs.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #15 → #19. The unbeaten start keeps Michigan in view; the next comparison must be tougher.

teams.reason: An enormous rebound is still a rebound. July’s No. 4 needs rebuilding.
teams.case: Oregon answered with a shutout and overwhelming production.
teams.doubt: An FCS rout cannot repair the meaning of the earlier loss by itself.
teams.proof: Beat a strong conference opponent before reclaiming elite billing.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #4 → #20. An enormous rebound is still a rebound. July’s No. 4 needs rebuilding.

teams.reason: Unbeaten gets Missouri onto the board; ten points keeps the claim modest.
teams.case: Three wins provide a firmer starting point than preseason omission.
teams.doubt: The latest margin offers little evidence of a large ceiling.
teams.proof: Create separation without relying on the opponent to run out of possessions.
teams.movementReason: New to PointCast 25. Unbeaten gets Missouri onto the board; ten points keeps the claim modest.

teams.reason: A road SEC result deserves space before brand familiarity takes it back.
teams.case: Winning in Columbia gives the unbeaten start a useful conference receipt.
teams.doubt: Thirty-one conceded leaves plenty of room for the next opponent.
teams.proof: Repeat the road composure while reducing the defensive exposure.
teams.movementReason: New to PointCast 25. A road SEC result deserves space before brand familiarity takes it back.

teams.reason: The loss changes the position; it does not erase the entire case.
teams.case: Thirty-one points on the road preserve a reason to keep watching the offense.
teams.doubt: Allowing forty-one is the clearest item on the repair list.
teams.proof: Win the next close game by getting a stop rather than demanding another score.
teams.movementReason: New to PointCast 25. The loss changes the position; it does not erase the entire case.

teams.reason: A home loss spends most of the preseason benefit of the doubt.
teams.case: The remaining winning record keeps a narrow place on this board.
teams.doubt: Losing by ten at home makes the finishing question more urgent.
teams.proof: Produce a response against serious opposition before asking for renewed trust.
teams.movementReason: Board 000: #13 → #24. A home loss spends most of the preseason benefit of the doubt.

teams.reason: A two-point road loss earns a closer look than a binary win column.
teams.case: Houston stayed within one score of an unbeaten ranked conference opponent.
teams.doubt: Competitive defeat still leaves the defining win uncollected.
teams.proof: Turn the next close conference chance into an actual result.
teams.movementReason: New to PointCast 25. A two-point road loss earns a closer look than a binary win column.
